outcome: Design, use and evaluate computational abstractions that model real-world problems and physical systems.
Understand key algorithms, such as sorting and searching, and compare alternatives with logical reasoning.
Use two or more programming languages, at least one textual, to solve a variety of problems.
Use data structures like lists, tables or arrays, and design modular programs with procedures or functions.
Understand simple Boolean logic (AND, OR, NOT) and its uses in circuits and programming.
Represent numbers in binary and do simple binary addition and binary-decimal conversion.
Understand the hardware and software components of computer systems and how they communicate.
Understand how instructions are stored and executed in a computer.
Understand how text, sound and pictures are represented and manipulated as binary digits.
Combine multiple applications across devices in creative projects that collect and analyse data for known users.
Create, re-use, revise and re-purpose digital artefacts for an audience, considering trustworthiness, design and usability.
Use technology safely, respectfully, responsibly and securely, protecting online identity and privacy.
Recognise inappropriate content, contact and conduct, and know how to report concerns.
Develop capability, creativity and knowledge in computer science, digital media and information technology.
Develop analytic, problem-solving, design and computational thinking skills.
Understand how changes in technology affect safety, including new ways to protect online privacy and identity.
Identify and report a range of concerns.
